3	Document-level relation extraction (DocRE) requires identifying semantic relations between entity pairs across multiple sentences, a task where encoder-based methods such as \citet{zhou2021atlop} long dominated.
4	Recent LLM-based approaches have closed this gap: \citet{autore2024} fine-tune LLMs with structured decomposition, \citet{xu2024lmrc} frame it as multi-choice reading comprehension, and \citet{xu2025docksrag} combine retrieval-augmented generation with structured knowledge.

6	Without evidence, a clinician reviewing a ten-page case report must manually locate the sentences that support each extracted drug interaction, a bottleneck that undermines trust in automated extraction.

## Part 0: Paper Information

**Title:**
Evidence at What Cost? Decoupling and Scaling in LLM-Based Document Relation Extraction

**Abstract:**
Large Language Model (LLM)-based Document-level Relation Extraction (DocRE) now matches or exceeds encoder baselines in extraction accuracy, yet outputs bare relation triplets without identifying supporting sentences. Encoder-based evidence methods (SAIS, DREEAM) provide evidence but trail LLM approaches in accuracy, creating a gap between extraction performance and verifiability. We study evidence-grounded DocRE as structured generation and compare Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), and Rejection Sampling Fine-Tuning (RSFT) across three fully evaluated scales (1.7B, 4B, 8B) with 14B validation, two model families, and two datasets. The evidence tax—the extraction cost of generating evidence—is scale-dependent: beneficial at 1.7B (−5.63pp Ign-F1) but approximately neutral at ≥4B, challenging the assumption that evidence always harms accuracy. Gradient-based optimization amplifies evidence-extraction competition (GRPO catastrophic, DPO gradual), while RSFT avoids decoupling because discrete output selection structurally cannot exploit the extraction-evidence trade-off. We define the Evidence-Decoupling Ratio (EDCR) to quantify this misalignment, validated at per-relation level (ρ=−0.79, p<0.001). Our 1.7B RSFT model approaches 8B supervised fine-tuning (SFT) performance at 4.7× fewer parameters, and test-set evaluation preserves model ranking across all scales.

**TL;DR:**
Evidence generation in LLM-based DocRE is not uniformly harmful; RSFT avoids extraction-evidence decoupling that gradient methods cause, enabling a 1.7B model to approach 8B SFT performance.

**Keywords:**
document-level relation extraction, evidence grounding, rejection sampling fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, structured generation, evidence faithfulness

**Secondary Subject Area:** Machine Learning for NLP
